criteria.check: Read metrics.compute; every M1..M16 value is computed in Python from categorised transactions; draft node only passes the rendered table to the model.
Read every Metric constructor; each carries an evidence id list (M10/M13 empty only when value is None).
Read draft node: user prompt = account name, period, metrics table, policy table, guard feedback. No transactions.

Read guard/redraft loop; probed thread reuse (redraft budget and stale feedback carried over), n/a reasons quoted per prompt rule 5 (over-flagged), truncated memo (grounded). Did not run an adversarial search for under-flagging.

Read review interrupt and finalise; probed concurrent resume on one SQLite thread and a second --out run. Finalisation always needs a decision, but a second reviewer's decision is silently dropped and the evidence file beside an approved memo can be replaced by another run's.
Not reviewed in depth from the platform seat (categorise.py rules not read line by line).
Policy is packaged YAML, validated (ops, on_fail, when_missing, numeric thresholds, known metric ids); CI installs the wheel outside the repo and loads it.
Committed CSVs are generator output; but the SQLite checkpoint DB stores full raw transaction descriptions and is not gitignored, nor are Monzo import outputs unless named *.private.csv.

Read ingest.load_csv (columns, ISO dates, future dates, plain amounts, order, balance chain, duplicate ids). Probed CLI: non-UTF-8 CSV, missing file and malformed policy YAML end in raw tracebacks, not a clear refusal.
ci.yml runs ruff, pytest and evals with --llm fake, no secrets; permissions contents: read. Ran pytest (174 passed) and evals --llm fake (9/9 grounded, truth ok, exit 0).
Ran evals/run_evals.py --llm fake: nine archetype x profile cases match truth on M2,M5,M6,M7,M8,M11,M12,M13,M15. Only nine fixed seeds, not 'any' statement.
Read guard.check; no property-based search for under-flagged numbers run from this seat.

findings.claim: The real-model eval job is gated to run from main (line 29) and holds id-token: write (line 20), but checks out and executes arbitrary branch/commit code from the code_ref input (pip install -e . and evals/run_evals.py). Any branch's unreviewed code therefore runs with the ability to mint a GitHub OIDC token whose ref claim is refs/heads/main, which is exactly what the federation rule pinned to main is meant to prevent. code_ref and model are also interpolated directly into a run script at line 63 (script injection).
findings.repro: Push a branch whose evals/run_evals.py does: import os,urllib.request; print(urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(os.environ['ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL']+'&audience=https://api.anthropic.com', headers={'Authorization':'Bearer '+os.environ['ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN']})).read()). Dispatch 'Real-model evals' from main with code_ref=<that branch>: the branch code receives a main-scoped token. Fix: evaluate only main, or run branch code in a job without id-token and pass a short-lived credential from a separate trusted step; move inputs into env vars.

findings.claim: `python evals/run_evals.py --llm anthropic | tee evals-output.txt` runs under GitHub's default `bash -e {0}` shell (no `shell: bash`, so no pipefail): the step's status is tee's, so a truth mismatch (run_evals exit 1) or a crash still shows a green job. The published grounding/truth evidence task cannot fail.
findings.repro: Locally: bash -e -c 'python3 -c "raise SystemExit(1)" | tee /dev/null'; echo $?  -> 0. Fix: add `shell: bash` (adds -o pipefail) or `set -o pipefail` to the step.

findings.claim: redrafts and guard_feedback are never reset at the start of a run (load node at line 193 does not set them; draft carries s.get('redrafts')). With a durable checkpointer and a reused --thread name (cli.py:70, 'Name this review'), a new run inherits the previous run's redraft count and rejection text: the model is told its (non-existent) previous draft was rejected and gets zero redrafts. Stale review and final_memo also remain in state.
findings.repro: Scratch probe probe_thread.py: run 1 on thread T with a hallucinating model -> redrafts 2, 3 LLM calls; run 2 on the same thread and SQLite db -> 'prompt carries guard_feedback: True', redrafts 2, 1 LLM call, stale review present. Fix: load returns {'redrafts': 0, 'guard_feedback': '', 'review': None, 'final_memo': None}, or refuse a thread id that already has a checkpoint.

findings.claim: The evidence file name is derived from --out regardless of outcome, so a rejected run writes NAME.rejected.md but overwrites NAME.evidence.json. An approved NAME.md from an earlier run then sits beside evidence recording a different reviewer, decision and inputs, while its appendix says the evidence for it is 'in the .evidence.json file written beside this memo'.
findings.repro: Scratch probe probe_cli.py: cma run examples/cafe_stretched.csv --vat-stagger 1 --reviewer 'A. Analyst' --yes --out memo.md; then cma run ... --vat-stagger 3 --reviewer 'B. Other' --out memo.md answering n. memo.md still says 'APPROVED by A. Analyst'; memo.evidence.json now has reviewer B. Other, approved false, vat_stagger 3. Fix: name evidence after the target (memo.rejected.evidence.json) and refuse to overwrite an existing approved pair.

findings.claim: Two reviewers who `cma resume` the same pending review on a shared --checkpoint-db both see the interrupt; the second Command(resume=...) on an already-finalised thread is a no-op that returns the first reviewer's final state. The second reviewer's decision is silently discarded and, at line 160, their CLI reports and writes (to their --out) the other person's approval. No compare-and-set on the checkpoint; no error.
findings.repro: Scratch probe probe_race.py: two SqliteSaver connections, both get_state(...).interrupts True; A resumes approved, B resumes approved=False -> B's returned final_memo is 'APPROVED by A. Approver'. Fix: re-check get_state(cfg).interrupts immediately before invoking and compare checkpoint_id; refuse if it moved.

findings.claim: Prompt rule 5 tells the model to give an n/a metric's reason from the method column, but method texts contain numbers the guard rejects: M13 without --vat-stagger (the CLI default) reads 'VAT stagger group not given (1, 2 or 3, ...)' (metrics.py:202) and M4 for short statements reads 'Needs at least six covered months' (metrics.py:150). A real model that obeys the prompt produces an ungrounded memo on the default invocation, burns both redrafts and reaches the reviewer marked not grounded, so overrides become routine. FakeLLM never writes the reason, so CI cannot see this.
findings.repro: Scratch probe probe_guard.py: memo 'Late or missed VAT payments are n/a [M13]: <M13.method>' with vat_stagger=None -> grounded False, unmatched '2','3', missing citation M7; 'Revenue trend is n/a [M4]: Needs at least six covered months...' -> unmatched 'six'. Fix: digit-free method texts for n/a cases, or exempt the method text when it follows its own n/a tag.

findings.claim: When the export has a Balance column and the user also passes --opening-balance, the walked balance is never checked against Monzo's Balance (check is limited to source == 'Monzo Balance column'). A wrong opening balance silently shifts every balance, so M5 (lowest balance) and M6 (days overdrawn, R4 policy) are wrong although the file contained the data to catch it.
findings.repro: Scratch probe probe_monzo.py: 3-row export with Balance 100, -200, 200; convert(..., opening_balance=5000) succeeds, balances 5100, 4800, 5200 (no overdrawn day). Fix: always cross-check when a Balance value is present.

findings.claim: AnthropicLLM ignores stop_reason (max_tokens=1500, no timeout set) and the guard checks only numbers, so a truncated memo with no Recommendation or policy outcome is 'grounded' and is approvable with --yes. Provider errors are not caught anywhere (cli.py:80 catches only StatementError/PolicyError).
findings.repro: PYTHONPATH=src python3 -c: FakeLLM subclass returning the memo cut before '## Cash position' -> guard grounded True, 'Recommendation' absent, redrafts 0.

findings.claim: Only StatementError and PolicyError are turned into a clear refusal. A Windows-1252 CSV (common for UK Excel exports with £), a missing statement path and malformed policy YAML end in raw UnicodeDecodeError / FileNotFoundError / yaml ParserError tracebacks; ingest opens utf-8-sig only (ingest.py:56).
findings.repro: Scratch probe probe_cli.py: cp1252 CSV -> exit 1 UnicodeDecodeError; nope.csv -> FileNotFoundError; 'rules: [' policy -> ParserError.

findings.claim: The --checkpoint-db SQLite file stores the full Statement including raw transaction descriptions (verified 'PARKGATE ESTATES' in the checkpoints/writes tables), with no retention or delete command, and neither *.sqlite/*.db nor memo/evidence outputs nor `cma import monzo -o` outputs are ignored unless named *.private.csv or under private/. A pilot run in the repo directory can commit a lender's statement.
findings.repro: Run probe_race.py, then scan race.sqlite tables for b'PARKGATE' -> True. git status would show the .sqlite as untracked, not ignored.
